The **University of St Andrews** ([Scots](/wiki/Scots_language "Scots language"): *University o St Andras*, [Scottish Gaelic](/wiki/Scottish_Gaelic_language "Scottish Gaelic language"): *Oilthigh Chill Rìmhinn*;[[6]](#cite_note-6) abbreviated as **St And** in [post-nominals](/wiki/Post-nominals "Post-nominals")[[a]](#cite_note-7)) is a [public](/wiki/Public_university "Public university") [research university](/wiki/Research_university "Research university") in the town of [St Andrews](/wiki/St_Andrews "St Andrews") in [Scotland](/wiki/Scotland "Scotland"). It is the [oldest](/wiki/List_of_oldest_universities_in_continuous_operation "List of oldest universities in continuous operation") of the four [ancient universities of Scotland](/wiki/Ancient_universities_of_Scotland "Ancient universities of Scotland") and, following the universities of [Oxford](/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford") and [Cambridge](/wiki/University_of_Cambridge "University of Cambridge"), the third-oldest university in the [English-speaking world](/wiki/English-speaking_world "English-speaking world"). St Andrews was founded in 1413 when the [Avignon](/wiki/Avignon_Pope "Avignon Pope") [Antipope Benedict XIII](/wiki/Antipope_Benedict_XIII "Antipope Benedict XIII") issued a [papal bull](/wiki/Papal_bull "Papal bull") to a small founding group of [Augustinian](/wiki/Augustinians "Augustinians") clergy. Along with the universities of [Glasgow](/wiki/University_of_Glasgow "University of Glasgow"), [Aberdeen](/wiki/University_of_Aberdeen "University of Aberdeen"), and [Edinburgh](/wiki/University_of_Edinburgh "University of Edinburgh"), St Andrews was part of the [Scottish Enlightenment](/wiki/Scottish_Enlightenment "Scottish Enlightenment") during the 18th century.

Jemulpo in 1890

Another historical name of the city, **Jemulpo** (alternatively Romanized as **Chemulpo**), was not widely used until the opening of the port in 1883. It was frequently used until the Japanese annexation.[[8]](#cite_note-9)[[9]](#cite_note-10) After the opening of the Incheon port, the city center moved from Gwangyo to Jemulpo. Today, either Jemulpo or Gwangyo-dong is considered "Original Incheon" (원인천). It was internationally known as **Jinsen** during [Japanese rule](/wiki/Korea_under_Japanese_rule "Korea under Japanese rule"), based on the Japanese pronunciation of Incheon's Sino-Korean name.

In 1914, the Japanese colonial government merged outer parts of old Incheon (including the former center of Gwangyo) with [Bupyeong](/wiki/Bupyeong_District "Bupyeong District") County, forming [Bucheon](/wiki/Bucheon "Bucheon") County.[[10]](#cite_note-11) Between 1936 and 1940, some part of Bucheon County was recombined into Incheon, by which some part of "old" Bupyeong was annexed into Incheon.

Incheon was originally part of [Gyeonggi Province](/wiki/Gyeonggi_Province "Gyeonggi Province"), but was granted *Directly Governed* (now Metropolitan) City status on 1 July 1981; the city officially separated from the province. In 1989, neighboring islands and Gyeyang township of Gimpo County[[b]](#cite_note-12) were ceded to Incheon and in 1995 Geomdan township of Gimpo County and two counties of Ganghwa and Onjin were annexed to Incheon.

Incheon was known as **Inchon** prior to South Korea's adoption of a [new Romanization system](/wiki/Revised_Romanization_of_Korean "Revised Romanization of Korean") in 2000.[[11]](#cite_note-13)

Founded in 1762, Allentown is located on the [Lehigh River](/wiki/Lehigh_River "Lehigh River"), a 109-mile-long (175 km) tributary of the [Delaware River](/wiki/Delaware_River "Delaware River"). It is the largest of three adjacent cities, including [Bethlehem](/wiki/Bethlehem,_Pennsylvania "Bethlehem, Pennsylvania") and [Easton](/wiki/Easton,_Pennsylvania "Easton, Pennsylvania") in Lehigh and [Northampton](/wiki/Northampton_County,_Pennsylvania "Northampton County, Pennsylvania") counties, in the Lehigh Valley region.[[13]](#cite_note-13) Allentown is located 48 miles (77 km) north of [Philadelphia](/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") and 78 miles (126 km) west of [New York City](/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").
